inputs.alt: The public release workflow shows 720 minutes of core QA, 480 minutes of reporting QA, and the original deadline beside an uncalculated Decision summary.
inputs.caption: Forms keeps the original workload and promise visible. Calculate evaluates the four supplied arrangements; Jira data does not supply the separate operating records.

baseline.alt: Only the full release with additional qualified QA passes the baseline. It costs $400 and is ready Monday at 5 p.m.; the other three arrangements remain visible with their commitment basis.
baseline.caption: The baseline admits one arrangement preserving the original scope and deadline. This model compares feasibility and declares no ranking or selected arrangement.

scopeBefore.alt: Core-only is ready Monday at 1 p.m. but is blocked because deferring reporting has not been explicitly accepted. The original scope and deadline remain displayed.
scopeBefore.caption: Finishing core work is different from fulfilling the original promise. Before the change is accepted, core-only remains blocked.

stale.alt: Recording acceptance of the reporting deferral marks the old calculation stale until Recalculate is used.
stale.caption: A changed amendment fact needs a new calculation. The previous finding does not remain current.

scopeAfter.alt: After acceptance is recorded and recalculated, the core-only arrangement is usable as an accepted scope revision. The report still says it does not preserve the original scope and deadline.
scopeAfter.caption: The same core-only schedule becomes an accepted revised commitment. It still does not deliver the reporting feature originally promised.

wrongBuildSummary.alt: No supplied arrangement passes when the only changed fact is that the additional QA qualification covers another build. The scope and later-date revisions remain unaccepted.
wrongBuildSummary.caption: The same headcount and $400 fee no longer provide a supported commitment. The qualification must cover the actual build and validation interval.

wrongBuild.alt: The additional-help arrangement is blocked by the scoped qualification condition when the external record names another build. Its fee and handoff time remain the same.
wrongBuild.caption: The decisive condition is a qualification covering this build, environment and actual work—not merely an available additional tester.

qualifiedHelp.alt: With the correct scoped qualification restored, the complete additional-help arrangement passes. It preserves the original release for $400, with a Monday 5 p.m. handoff.
qualifiedHelp.caption: Qualified help makes one supplied complete arrangement feasible. It is not a generic rule that any extra person saves a release.

helpTiming.alt: The Work and timing report shows the additional QA resource performing the fixed independent regression phase while the existing QA allocation performs the remaining authored work.
helpTiming.caption: The model transfers a fixed independent-regression package. Other phases and their dependencies remain with the authored resources.

process.alt: The actual release decision graph connects calculability, passing original-commitment arrangements, accepted revisions and reconsideration of the recorded basis.
process.caption: The process keeps recovering the original release separate from adopting a different commitment. Inspecting a path neither accepts an amendment nor deploys software.
